summary: Robert Alexander Neil was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Aberdeen and Cambridge under Geddes, Cowell, Verrall, Reid, and Shilleto. He was a Fellow and Senior Tutor at Pembroke College and Cambridge University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1883-1901).

Robert Anderson was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He was educated at Harrow School and the East India Company College (~1807-1809), where he later served as an Assistant Professor from 1821 to 1825.

Robert Anthony Orsi works in religious studies and history/archaeology. Educated at Trinity College and Yale, he held posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard, Northwestern (holding the Grace Craddock Nagle Chair from ~2007), and Notre Dame.

Robert Antoine was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Calcutta (~1948-1950). He founded Shanti Bhavan in 1950, taught Sanskrit at St. Xavier's, and became Reader at Jadavpur University in 1956.

Robert Arrowsmith worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Columbia and Berlin, he taught at Columbia, Racine College, and Teachers College, served as principal of Barnard School and Erasmus Hall High School, and was an editor for the American Book Company.

Robert Atkinson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Trinity College Dublin and the University of Liège. He served as Professor of Romance Languages at Trinity College Dublin, taught at Trinity College, Hartford, and presided over the Royal Irish Academy.

Robert Baker Aitken worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Educated at the University of Hawaiʻi and UC Berkeley, he studied under D. T. Suzuki and multiple Zen masters. He founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha and the Buddhist Peace Fellowship.
Robert Barkley Shaw worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as linguistics. He completed his education at Marlborough College (~1853-1858) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1858-1859).

Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge and founded the Tibet Information Network. He held positions at Columbia University (~1999-2018), Tibet University, SOAS, and King's College London.

Robert Bleichsteiner was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Vienna under Bittner, von Schroeder, and Geiger, he became Director of the Weltmuseum Wien in 1945 and a Vienna professor in 1947.

Robert Boxberger was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under August Schleicher at the University of Jena (1855-1858). He worked as a teacher at Realschule Erfurt (1858-1876) and a librarian at the Herzogin Anna Amalia Bibliothek (1868-1876).

Robert Brainerd Ekvall was a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and other fields. He studied at Wheaton College, Nyack College, and the University of Chicago, later holding posts at Chicago, the University of Washington, and the Burke Museum.

Robert Bruce Foote was a history and archaeology specialist. He served as Superintendent at the Geological Survey of India (1858-1891), worked in Baroda State (1892), and became Director of the Mysore Geological Department in 1894.

Robert Caesar Childers was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yatramulle Dhammarama, he served at the India Office Library and became Professor of Pali and Buddhist literature at University College London.

Robert Chalmers was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Oriel College, Oxford, under Edwin Abbott Abbott and T. W. Rhys Davids, he served as President of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922-1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924-1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indology and law scholar educated at Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford, Principal of New Inn Hall, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, and President of The Asiatic Society.

Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and under H. W. Bailey at Cambridge, he became Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics at Oxford in 1952.

Robert Cotton Mather was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his education at the University of Edinburgh, the University of Glasgow (earning an M.A. by 1831), and Homerton College (~1831-1833).

Robert DeCaroli is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at UCLA under Katherine Anne Harper and Robert L. Brown, and later held teaching posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount University, and George Mason University.

Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1978-1983). He has held academic posts at the University of Kerala and the Université catholique de Louvain, where he became a professor around 1989.
